(1) Neighborhood #1
(See "Project Neighborhoods," Part II, paragraph 5.) The character of this neighborhood will be affected by the plan. The scheduled redevelopment along Front Street is part of the plan to convert the area to a more residential character.
Changes in the zoning of the area for business/commercial to residential will likewise change neighborhood character. The object of this is to stem the commercial development before such development reaches a point past which control is lost over commercial building within the 100 year flood plain. In this regard, a major positive value is given this factor, as it relates to flood planning.
The architectural character of the area will vary little from the latest contemporary buildings presently found in the area; however, as mentioned in Part II, the new building in the area will conform to the proposed flood plain ordinance. These new requirements could force a change in the neighborhood's architectural scheme. Whether or not this expected change is a positive factor, as it relates to aesthetics, can not be determined at this time.
(2) Neighborhood #2
This area will experience some changes in character. It will become less commercial and less densely populated, but it will retain some neighborhood shopping. The aesthetics of the neighborhood should be improved by this action. This would be seen, not so much in the construction of new buildings, but in the removal of a number of structures which now give the area a very shabby appearance.
The architectural scheme of this neighborhood could change, somewhat, due to the amount of acquisition and land reuse scheduled.
(3) Neighborhood #3
The overall character of this neighborhood will not be altered; however the blighting influences of property deterioration and over-population will be removed. Removal of these adverse items will contribute to the existing positive character of the area, without destroying its overall character. Due to the concentration of rehabilitation efforts in the area, and the use of code enforcement measures, the present architectural character will be preserved.
